name: How do I choose materials for a high-traffic office renovation?

mainEntity.name: Which flooring, wall finishes, and fixtures hold up best in busy office spaces with heavy daily use?
mainEntity.text: Which flooring, wall finishes, and fixtures hold up best in busy office spaces with heavy daily use?

acceptedAnswer.text: High-traffic office spaces need materials that can handle rolling chairs, foot traffic, cleaning, and long daily use without looking worn too quickly. Commercial carpet tile is popular because damaged sections can be replaced individually. Luxury vinyl tile works well in reception areas and corridors because it is durable and easy to clean. Porcelain tile, high-pressure laminate, and impact-resistant wall protection can help in areas that take more abuse. For workstations and shared spaces, choose finishes that are both easy to maintain and visually consistent under strong lighting. The best material package depends on whether the priority is acoustics, appearance, durability, or all three. Contractors should also confirm that selected materials meet fire-rating, slip-resistance, and maintenance requirements for the building.
acceptedAnswer.description: For high-traffic office renovations, durable materials like commercial-grade carpet tile, luxury vinyl tile, porcelain, high-pressure laminate, and washable paint usually perform better than residential-grade finishes. The best choices balance durability, maintenance, acoustics, and budget.
